week.weeklyOverview: Toddlers explore apples as real fruit—looking, touching, smelling, sorting colors, and (with allergy checks) tasting. The week mixes short science looks, large-motor apple hunts, market pretend play, and process art that does not repeat the same stamp craft every day. Teachers keep experiences repeatable and washable, celebrate crunchy vocabulary, and offer non-food alternatives whenever tasting is not appropriate.
week.weeklyMaterials:
Real red, green, and yellow apples (whole)
Prepared apple slices for supervised taste test (allergy-checked)
Plastic play apples and baskets
Apple picture / color cards
Magnifying glasses (plastic)
Washable red/green/yellow paint and smocks
Apple-shaped sponges OR cookie cutters (vary art tools across days)
Construction paper, crayons, glue sticks, dot markers
Play dough and apple-sized balls
Sensory bin filler alternative: crumpled paper “orchard leaves” with plastic apples (no water beads)
Bean bags and floor spots for relays
Toy market stand props
Chart paper for favorite-apple graph
Wipes, towels, and labeled allergy notes
week.teacherPreparation: Prep one tray at a time at toddler height. Keep Apples materials chunky, washable, and mouthing-safe.
week.familyConnection: At the store or fridge, invite your child to find a red, green, or yellow apple and describe how it feels. If allergies allow, taste a slice together and talk about sweet, crunchy, or juicy. No orchard trip required—window shopping the produce aisle still builds rich apple talk.
milestones: Language: Uses apple color and sensory words (red, crunch, stem, sweet) during play and tasting talk
SEL: Waits for a turn with apples/baskets and tries a new food experience with supportive coaching
Motor: Stamps/sponges, carries baskets, rolls, and sorts oversized apple props
Cognition: Sorts apples by color/size and notices simple tree-to-fruit ideas with picture support

songs.title: Apple Colors Chant
songs.motions: Hold up matching color cards; pretend pick; rub-shine motion; tap count to three.
songs.teacherDirections: Use real or play apples as visual anchors. Invite each toddler to show a color rather than answer verbally if needed.
songs.whenToUse: Monday circle with the apple basket reveal; Apple Color Sort warm-up
songs.transitionPurpose: Focus attention on apple colors before investigation
songs.lyrics:
Red apple, green apple, yellow too,
Pick one up—which color are you?
Shine and wash and count with me,
Apples for our friends to see.

songs.title: Crunch, Munch, Pause
songs.motions: Tap fists together for crunch; wipe mouth politely for munch; hands in lap on take our time; thank-you wave.
songs.teacherDirections: Sing before Apple Taste Test. Emphasize that touching/smelling is a full participate option. Never pressure tasting.
songs.whenToUse: Taste-test preview and mealtime apple talk
songs.transitionPurpose: Set calm tasting manners and inclusion norms
songs.lyrics:
Crunch, crunch, listen close,
Munch, munch—politely most.
Taste or touch, we take our time,
Thank you, apples—you’re so fine!

songs.title: Roll, Pick, Parade
songs.motions: Seated rock/roll arms; reach high/low pick; pretend carry basket; march in place.
songs.teacherDirections: Bridge Roll Like an Apple and Apple Basket Relay. Keep rolls seated or crawling—no tumbling piles.
songs.whenToUse: Gross-motor apple days and Friday harvest celebration
songs.transitionPurpose: Move from floor play into cleanup or parade
songs.lyrics:
Roll like an apple, round we go,
Pick the apples high and low.
Basket full—we march and sing,
Harvest friends, hear us ring!

books.title: Apple Farmer Annie
books.author: Monica Wellington
books.whyThisBook: Bright orchard-to-market sequence helps toddlers connect apples to growing, sorting, and sharing food.
beforeReadingQuestions: Where do you think Annie’s apples grow?
duringReadingPrompts: What is Annie doing with the apples on this page?
afterReadingQuestions: Would you like to pick, wash, or sell apples in pretend play?
books.substituteTitle: Apple picture cards plus Apple Colors Chant if the book is unavailable.

books.title: Apples and Pumpkins
books.author: Anne Rockwell
books.whyThisBook: Seasonal farm visit text supports fall apple talk with clear, toddler-friendly illustrations.
beforeReadingQuestions: Have you seen an apple tree or pumpkin patch?
duringReadingPrompts: Can you find the apples in the picture?
afterReadingQuestions: What would you put in your harvest basket?
books.substituteTitle: Outdoor apple hunt with plastic apples and basket counting.

books.title: How Do Apples Grow?
books.author: Betsy Maestro
books.whyThisBook: Simple nonfiction explains blossom-to-fruit ideas that pair with Apple Life Cycle and seed discovery.
beforeReadingQuestions: What do you think an apple needs to grow?
duringReadingPrompts: Point to the flower, the tiny apple, or the tree.
afterReadingQuestions: How can we take care of living growing things?
books.substituteTitle: Three life-cycle picture cards (flower, tiny apple, ripe apple) for a mini sequence talk.

books.title: Ten Apples Up On Top!
books.author: Theo LeSieg
books.whyThisBook: Playful counting and balancing humor enriches number talk; use selectively for short read-alouds.
duringReadingPrompts: How many apples are on top now?
afterReadingQuestions: Let’s count five play apples into a basket.
books.substituteTitle: Optional enrichment title—fully use if time allows; otherwise keep counting with real props.

books.title: The Biggest Apple Ever
books.author: Steven Kroll
books.whyThisBook: Friendship-and-size story supports big/small apple comparisons without requiring a full week slot.
beforeReadingQuestions: What makes an apple look big?
duringReadingPrompts: Who is trying to find the biggest apple?
afterReadingQuestions: Can you find a big apple and a small apple in our basket?
books.substituteTitle: Optional fifth title for family lending or quiet shelf; prioritize top three for circle.

teacherToolkit.teacherPreparation: Prep one tray at a time at toddler height. Keep Apples materials chunky, washable, and mouthing-safe.
prepChecklist: Set materials at child height before arrival
Place cleanup caddy near the play space
Review allergy and supervision notes for the day
observationFocus: Persists with a material or peer exchange
Shows interest or curiosity during invitations
observationPrompts: What language or gestures appear during play?
How does the child enter and leave the invitation?
Where do peers support or extend the idea?
documentationPrompts: Capture one moment of child-led exploration (with permission).
Note a verbatim quote or gesture tied to the theme.
teacherTips: Model once, then narrate what you notice.
Offer two choices instead of open-ended demands.
Keep transitions short with a familiar song cue.
setupCleanupShortcuts: Trays labeled and stacked by day
Damp cloth + bin for quick reset
Spare substitution basket on the shelf

materialSubstitutions.use: printed picture cards or recycled clean containers

teacherToolkit.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger toddlers explore with larger pieces; older peers get a second sorting rule or helper job.
teacherToolkit.extraSupportAdaptations: Sit beside, shorten the invitation, and offer hand-under-hand only when welcomed.
teacherToolkit.challengeExtensions: Invite children to invent a new Apples rule, map, or story for peers.
teacherToolkit.safetyInclusionNotes: Confirm allergies before any apple tasting and provide equal non-tasting roles. Wash produce and hands; keep cut pieces refrigerated per program food rules. Avoid water beads and small loose seeds as play fillers. Art uses washable paint with smocks; vary tools so stamp painting is not daily. Supervise baskets/relays for safe carrying. Include children who cannot eat apples through smell, touch, sort, and pretend market play.
teacherToolkit.endOfWeekReflection: Which Apples words and strategies showed up most in play?
teacherToolkit.familyConnection: Share one Apples word or song to try at home during ordinary routines.
teacherToolkit.notes: Draft toolkit for owner review — enrichment draft only.

legacySnapshot.weeklyOverview: This week, toddlers will explore the wonderful world of apples through hands-on investigations, sensory experiences, movement, music, dramatic play, art, and early science activities. Children will discover that apples come in different colors, sizes, and tastes while learning where apples grow and how they become healthy foods we can enjoy. Throughout the week, they will strengthen language skills, early math concepts, fine and gross motor development, and social-emotional skills by working together during engaging apple-themed experiences.
legacySnapshot.objectives:
Identify apples as a healthy fruit.
Recognize red, green, and yellow apples.
Explore apples using the five senses.
Compare apples by size, color, and texture.
Practice counting, sorting, and matching apples.
Strengthen fine motor skills through art and sensory play.
Build vocabulary related to apples and orchards.
Encourage curiosity through simple science investigations.
Participate in cooperative play and group discussions.
Develop confidence while exploring new foods and experiences.
